newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek tax revenue growth below goal in Jan-Feb - min.
newsitem.headline: Greek tax revenue growth below goal in Jan-Feb - min.

text.p: Greece's Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said tax revenues in the first two months of 1997 grew by less than 14.6 percent, against a budgeted target of 14.9 percent for the year as a whole.
Tax revenues rose 14.2 percent in January and press reports said they increased by a meagre 6.5 percent in February.
Drys declined to specify the exact tax revenue figure for February.

The deputy finance minister told Reuters that VAT revenues were lagging behind target in February because 30 percent of VAT payers would actually pay it in March due to a change in the VAT collection system.
The finance ministry used to collect the VAT on an alphabetical order system but switched to a new system based on taxpayers' identification codes this year, he said.
Greece's general government budget deficit is projected to fall to 4.2 percent of GDP in 1997 from an estimated 7.4 percent of GDP in 1996.
General government current spending is forecast to rise 5.8 percent and tax revenues by 14.9 percent in 1997.
